reader.requirement: At --std 85, a file SORT must order records by the KEY data-names taken left to right as decreasing significance regardless of how they are split into KEY phrases, ascending or descending per phrase, each key compared by the 1985 relation-condition rules: numeric keys (DISPLAY, SIGN SEPARATE, COMPUTATIONAL/BINARY, PACKED-DECIMAL, P-scaled) algebraically, nonnumeric keys (alphanumeric, numeric-edited, group) as character strings; a key described in only one of several record descriptions applies to every record; the edition has only the file format (no table SORT) and requires key data-names.

edition-consulted.switches: construct table-sort-2002 (COBOL0870): a SORT with no USING/INPUT/GIVING/OUTPUT phrase (the Format 2 table sort) is refused below 2002

reader.edition-search: Key binding and comparison (SortAddFileKeys, SortKeyColumns.Compare) read no edition: grep 'Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect' over SortKeyColumns.cs and SortEmitter.cs found nothing; SortBinder's ctx.Edition uses on this path are diagnostic sinks only. The edition arm is the Format 2 gate.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for file-SORT key ordering; yes for the statement's range: the table SORT (the SortBindTable/EmitTableSort seeds) is refused at 85 and accepted at 2023
